findings.question: Is _NodeReporter's output-truncation code path (the block adding `_truncate_content` calls) invoked exactly once per test report, or could it run multiple times across setup/call/teardown phases, causing an already-truncated section (including its marker text) to be re-sliced and produce a nested/duplicate truncation marker?
findings.why: The diff only shows one call site truncating content_out/content_log/content_err; if this helper is invoked per-phase rather than once on the final merged content, repeated truncation could corrupt or duplicate the marker, which is not covered by the current tests (tests only check single-phase stdout/stderr).

disposition.reason: Verified by running actual pytest (not just reading code): write_captured_output can be called up to twice per test (once at report.when=="call" via the `if not self.log_passing_tests: reporter.write_captured_output(report)` branch in pytest_runtest_logreport, src/_pytest/junitxml.py ~pytest_runtest_logreport, and once unconditionally at report.when=="teardown"), but the teardown call is always guarded by `if not self.xml.log_passing_tests and report.passed: return` at the top of write_captured_output (src/_pytest/junitxml.py write_captured_output). Empirically (python -m pytest --junitxml, junit_log_passing_tests=False, a failing test with an autouse fixture printing at teardown): only ONE <system-out> element is ever written, with no duplicate/nested truncation marker, in both the log_passing_tests=False (only call-phase write fires) and log_passing_tests=True (only teardown-phase write fires, using report.capstdout which is pytest's own pre-existing cumulative concatenation of all phases' "Captured stdout *" sections, unrelated to this change) cases. _truncate_content is therefore invoked at most once per section per test, never on already-truncated content, so no nested/duplicate marker is possible. No code change or decision needed.

nodes.question: Confirm the JUnit XML captured-output truncation design before shipping: ini option name `junit_logging_truncation_limit`, limit units = Unicode characters (not bytes), 0 = disabled (unlimited, backward compatible), and truncation marker text `\n...[N chars truncated]...\n` placed in the middle (keeping head+tail, applied uniformly to passing and failing tests, never truncating the failure/error longrepr itself).
nodes.answer: I want a few changes. Call the ini setting junit_output_limit. Default 0 means unlimited. Positive values keep the first N Unicode code points of each raw captured stdout, stderr and log section independently, before adding headers or XML escaping. If cut, append a newline, [... output truncated ...], then a newline; the marker and header do not count toward N. No tail retention. Apply this equally to passing and failing tests' captured streams. Preserve the complete failure/error traceback diagnostics, and preserve existing junit_logging and junit_log_passing_tests filtering. Reject negative and non-integer settings with a clear configuration error. This keeps CI output bounded without hiding why a test failed.
